To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Sgr B cloud has an average spectral index α = 0.5, a total mass M = 3 × 10^6 M_⊙, and a magnetic field strength of 0.5 mG, and that it is a site of ongoing star formation.

(1) the radio continuum emission of Sgr B is consistent with the presence of a compact radio core, and (2) the 1384 and the 2368 MHz images are consistent with a single, unresolved, compact radio source.
the 1384 MHz continuum emission from Sgr B is dominated by thermal emission from ionized gas and the 2368 MHz continuum is dominated by nonthermal emission from cosmic ray electrons.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: What are the physical properties of Sgr B2?
the physical properties of the interstellar medium in the Galactic Center region.
the study of the radio emission of the Sgr B complex and its environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Sgr B2 complex is a giant molecular cloud (GMC) of mass 2 x 10^6 Msun and diameter 100 pc in which the central 20 pc contains a cluster of massive stars and the central 1.6 pc contains a cluster with a black hole.
the 2368 MHz continuum is a superposition of a 1-2 mJy background source, the 1384 MHz continuum, and an additional 2-3 mJy source, which is probably associated with the HII region Sgr B2.
the Sgr B complex is a very complex region, and the 3D structure and kinematics of the Sgr B2 region in particular is still not fully understood.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the 1384 MHz observations of the Sgr B region show that the 5 GHz continuum emission is not due to thermal bremsstrahlung, but that the 2368 MHz observations show that it could be thermal bremsstrahlung from a hot, low-density ionized gas.
the 1384 and the 2368 MHz continuum images are consistent with the presence of two distinct populations of ionized gas in Sgr B.
the 2368 MHz observations of Sgr B are the best yet of a Galactic center molecular cloud.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Sgr B2 cloud is a very dynamic environment, with a large-scale velocity gradient, and a complex velocity structure.
we have detected radio continuum emission from the Sgr B2 giant molecular cloud, and that the 1384-MHz image shows a more complex morphology than the 2368-MHz image.
the 1384-MHz continuum emission is dominated by free-free emission.
